title: Fats fills the Howard Theater with neighborhood kids and candy
summary: Fats invited neighborhood kids to the show, bought a hundred pounds of candy, and filled the theater, threatening to walk out on the horrified manager, who then held the show over.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom

blocks.x: Quite often. Quite often. I'm trying to think of some more, but I've seen him do a lot of things that were so doggoned nice, and to other people, and -- I thought it was nice. Oh! In Washington, D. C., after we stopped doing sat down one night here, and started doing theaters, well he had three children then, and it was all, you know. I remember, we were in Philadelphia. This -- I really enjoy telling.

As he would come out, stage, backstage, out in the alley, well, out in the streets, trying to get some air, naturally he had to see people, hello professor. So a kid one day -- a kid walked up, and he spoke to him, because he loved kids. Can I see the show? Fats said, just a minute, what's your name, he told him. Uh-huh. Where do you live? He told him.

You have any boyfriends? Girlfriends? He said yeah. He says okay. Fats say, for instance, come back here Thursday, or whatever day it was, tell all the friends in your block that I say you bring them and come see the show.

Now, that one -- he told one kid, now when this kid goes back to the other kids and they come back to see if it was true, then another kid might come up and say well I want to go in and see the show. And Fats would tell him the same thing. He did that. When this particular day came, God dog! You never saw so many kids in all your life standing there.
Now the manager, the manager didn't know a damn thing about this arrangement, of the theater.
Fats hadn't said anything.

And this was Washington, D. C. The Howard Theater. So the people there -- so Fats told his valet, chauffeur, go out, go to the five and ten, go there and buy me 50 pounds, a hundred pounds of candy, bags, and put it all in bags, you know. And he did, and had it all, you know, had little bags of candy, and I don't know how many he had. He had them -- (laughs.)

And as the kids -- and the kids came up, somebody said where you going? said Fats told me to come up. Somebody came around in back and said Fats, come, they need you cut front, says, man, there's a thousand kids out there waiting (laughs). So the manager says, 'What's going on here?'
(Don't worry about it)
What are you doing? Fats says (unintelligible). Fats told him, said get the candy in bags and stand right by the door.

And the manager, 'What's going on here,' he say. The kids are coming, but who told me -- didn't know, he -- this can't happen. Fats said, 'Naw? He said I'll pull the band out. I'll walk out.' 'Wait! No! Wait! Wait!' The man started hollering and was going crazy.
(Laughter.)

So Fats said, Follow me! Fats walked in leading the kids, and as they walked down the aisle the guy was-- handed each one of them a bag of candy. You never saw so damn many kids in all your life. (Laughs.)

They went -- all went down to the front, you know, and fill all the seats. When that was filled they started going upstairs filling all the seats, and the rest of the people couldn't get in, nothing but kids, and kids and candy, and when the curtain went up, you know, you can imagine what happened.
Ra-a-a-y-y-y, Fats!
Fats play a good show?

Good show, and played to the kids, and sang to them, and all their requests, and asked them what they wanted, and played for them. And the kids were happy, and went out, and the manager was out there, and they were giving him salts, smelling salts, headache powders, aw!
(Laughter.)

The next day, and the rest of the week, in fact, they held him over. As far as you could look, parents, grandparents, everything, was standing in line. 'I never heard of this man. I must see the man who gave my son, grandson, a free ticket to the show. I've got to see him. He's got to be a good man.' 'I've heard of him, but I've got to see him.' And they were -- they were standing in line for miles, look like, around the corner, down the corner, trying to get in the theater, had to hold him over.
That's terrific. Did Pats do things with kids like this very often, or --
He, aw, everywhere, everywhere he could, and naturally, you know -- the manager was happy, oh, he was happy! You know. But I mean before that the manager was about to go out of his mind.
Right, well he didn't --
He let all those people in there, and nothing going in the cash register.
The greatest public relations in the world.
And he's paying Fats all that money.
Right.
He says how am I going to pay him?! You know. (Laughs.)
He found out.
Yeah. Yeah. And I thought that was beautiful. I thought that was one -- you know. The most wonderful gesture, thing, I'd ever seen in my life.
